title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Lane Survey. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Lane Survey
options.lineage: oil-pattern sheets and lane condition drawings bowlers actually read
options.thesis: The centre drawn as the measured object it is: 32 lit strips of maple on a dark house floor, time running down each one. Refuses the page every bowling site ships, a dark stock photo of a lane with a neon glow and a floating BOOK NOW.
materials: lacquered lane maple under house lights
drafting rule, board numbers, foul line
oil-pattern fill as the booked state
options.viewport: Near-black lacquer ground. 32 vertical lit maple strips run from the top of the viewport down past the fold. Time runs down each strip against a measured rule at the left edge in tabular figures. Booked stretches fill maroon; open stretches stay lit. The headline sits in the dark gutter margin, one line, and the primary action is the strips themselves: tap an open stretch to start booking. The proof and the action are the same object.
options.risk: A measured technical world can read clinical for a parent planning a seven-year-old birthday party. The warmth has to arrive as real photography of kids bowling set into the lit strips and in the copy voice. Weak photography turns this cold.

raised.raise: The page now has one true axial spine with a resolving vista: everything is measured down a single 60-foot axis and the sightline ends on the booking action, rather than scattering measured marks across independent sections.
The booking flow teaches its own rules warmly at the moment they bind. Minimum 2 lanes and 10 players is explained where it stops you, in plain language, never as fine print.
One construction rule governs every atom. Nav, footer, inputs and buttons are all drawn in the survey line weights and board numbering. No untreated stock chrome anywhere on the page.

options.label: The Scoresheet
options.lineage: the ten-frame scoresheet and the overhead scoring monitor
options.thesis: The whole site set in the notation every bowler reads without thinking: ten boxed frames, X and slash, running total.
options.viewport: The frame grid as the whole page structure, each frame a section, the running total carrying the booking state.
options.risk: This is my top-ranked candidate and it is also where most runs in this category land. The scoresheet is the first thing anyone reaches for when designing a bowling site, so it is strong, legible, and the least surprising thing on this table.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.lineage: broadcast teletext magazines, 40 by 24 on black
options.thesis: The centre as a broadcast index: lane availability as live figures keyed by page number.
options.viewport: P302 builds itself from cyan blocks: tonight lanes as live figures on flat black.
options.case: Holds product clarity outright. Teletext was the availability medium, football scores and schedules in a strict grid, and a lane board is exactly that. Loses audience identification: a young parent in Doha has no teletext memory, and the federation reads it as retro novelty rather than official.
options.risk: Reads as retro-novelty the moment the grid loosens, and the eight fixed broadcast colours cannot carry Qatar maroon.

options.label: Saul Bass Title Sequence
options.lineage: cut-paper title sequences on flat saturated fields
options.thesis: Bowling told as cut-paper silhouettes, one idea per card, the field colour swapping per act.
options.viewport: A black cut-paper arm swinging a ball across a full-bleed maroon field, one line of hand-set caps off baseline.
options.case: Holds audience identification: bowling own mid-century era matches Bass exactly, and the flat saturated field takes Qatar maroon perfectly. Loses product clarity: a timed card sequence fights a booking task. You cannot check tonight availability inside a title sequence, and the primary user came to do precisely that.
options.risk: The timed cards actively obstruct the one job the site exists to do.

options.label: Jacquard Punched Brocade
options.lineage: punch-card looms weaving binary instructions into a motif
options.thesis: Availability as a binary matrix: thousands of lift-or-skip decisions resolving into a readable pattern.
options.viewport: Rows of punched slots above, the woven availability motif gathering below.
options.case: Holds product clarity on a real structural match: a binary lift matrix and a lane-hour availability grid are the same data, and the loom dual representation gives an exact accessible text equivalent for free. Loses audience identification: nothing about a Doha bowling centre lives in a Lyon weaving shed, and the federation would read it as decoration.
options.risk: The structural match is invisible to every visitor who is not already looking for it.

options.label: Gardens of Versailles
options.case: Loses both axes. A Doha parent does not identify with French formal landscape, and axial garden rooms do not clarify lane availability.
options.kept: Axial choreography: one true spine with a sightline that resolves at a fixed point.

options.label: Hand-Drawn Zine Explainer
options.case: Loses both axes. Hand-drawn undermines the institutional credibility a state-owned federation venue needs, and prices, hours and availability demand a precision the form actively refuses.
options.kept: Teaching warmth: guide the visitor through a process with explicit friendly wayfinding at the moment a rule binds.

options.label: Chaekgeori Reverse Perspective
options.lineage: painted bookshelf screens opening toward the viewer
options.case: Loses both axes. The audience has no relationship to Joseon shelf painting, and a perceptual trick that makes space feel wrong is the opposite of what a booking task needs.
options.kept: The courage of a single perceptual construction carried across every component without exception.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What every bowling centre site ships, executed impeccably: full-bleed lane photo, neon glow, big BOOK NOW, three feature cards, a party package grid.
canonCard.viewport: A dark hero photo of a lane with the headline centred over it and a single amber button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every competitor by design, and it makes the pitch an argument about taste rather than about bookings.
